back: A diagram of the options open to a decision maker, the possible outcomes of each, their probabilities and money values, used to compare the options.
The sum of each possible outcome multiplied by its probability; the average result if the decision were repeated many times.
Net expected value = expected value − cost of the option. Choose the highest.
Square = a decision the business makes. Circle = an event outside its control, with probabilities on the branches.
The probabilities on the branches leaving one chance node always add up to 1.
Start at the last decision on the right, use its net value as an outcome, and work back to the first decision on the left.
